title: Big and small black holes follow the same rule
summary:
Black holes come in very different sizes. Some weigh about 10 times as much as the Sun. Others weigh millions of times more. Scientists now say both kinds follow the same rule when they shoot jets of material into space.

The study was led by Dr. Adelle Goodwin in Australia and Dr. Andrew Mummery in Princeton.

The team studied times when a giant black hole pulls a star apart. Sometimes a jet shoots out right away. Other times, the jet appears months or even years later. Why?

The scientists found that late jets appear when the black hole's "eating" slows down to a certain point. Smaller black holes make jets at that same point.

Not everything near a black hole falls in. Some material blasts back out. Goodwin called it "a black hole burp."

The rule could help scientists predict when these outbursts will happen.
why_it_matters: Finding one rule for black holes of all sizes helps us understand how the universe around us works.

keywords.explanation: Black holes are places in space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can get out.
Jets are fast, narrow streams of material shooting out into space.
Material is the stuff that things are made of, like gas and dust in space.
To predict means to say what will happen before it happens.

Some black holes are small, and others are giant ones found in the middle of galaxies.
When gas or pieces of a star swirl around a black hole, some of it can shoot back out into space as a jet.
